# Financial and Strategic Analysis of the Company

## Introduction

The course **Financial and Strategic Analysis of the Company** is part of the
first skills block, **Designing the financial and non-financial strategy of
organisations**, of the [Expert en Stratégie Financière (RNCP40177)](https://www.francecompetences.fr/recherche/rncp/40177/)
title (Expert in Financial Strategy), recognised by
[France Compétences](https://www.francecompetences.fr/).

It is offered to students of the INSEEC **Master of Science** programmes
[Finance d'Entreprise & Ingénierie Financière](https://www.inseec.com/program/msc-finance-dentreprise-ingenierie-financiere/)
(Corporate Finance & Financial Engineering),
[Manager Financier, Banque & Assurance](https://www.inseec.com/program/msc-manager-financier-banque-assurance/)
(Financial Manager, Banking & Insurance),
[Banque d'Affaires & Ingénierie Financière](https://www.inseec.com/program/msc-banque-daffaires-ingenierie-financiere/)
(Investment Banking & Financial Engineering)
and [Analyse Financière Internationale](https://www.inseec.com/program/msc-analyse-financiere-internationale-2/)
(International Financial Analysis). The module aims to develop in-depth
expertise in financial diagnosis, performance analysis and the design of
financial and non-financial strategies, in line with international standards
(IFRS, GAAP), ESG issues and regulatory requirements (CSRD, AMF, etc.).

The course builds on the operational methodology of the [Banque de France](banque-france.qmd),
as practised by its financial analysts in the [rating of companies](banque-france-cotation.qmd).
This methodology bases the analysis on the review of **consolidated accounts**
and relies on a **6-step** process applied to more than 5,000 groups every
year.

## The 6-step methodology

| Step | Content | Quests |
|:----:|---------|--------|
| **1** | Environment, strategy and organisation — SWOT, legal, economic and financial analysis | Q5 |
| **2** | Critical review of the information — consolidation scope, methods (full / proportionate consolidation / equity method), audit certification | Q2 |
| **3** | Analysis of [performance](performances.qmd) — recurring net income (RNR ≈ ¾ × RCAI, i.e. pre-tax ordinary income), trends, sector comparison | Q4 |
| **4** | [Financial structure](structure-fi.qmd) — FPNR (restated equity), goodwill assessment, restated debt, financial autonomy (CAF, i.e. cash flow) | Q3, Q4 |
| **5** | [Liquidity](liquidite.qmd) — static analysis (FRNG, net working capital / BFR, working-capital requirement), dynamic (FTA/CA), forward-looking (FTD over N+1, N+2), financial risks | Q3, Q8 |
| **6** | [Rating](banque-france-cotation.qmd) decision — financial rating, qualitative profile, outlook, recommendation for subsidiaries | Q3, Q6 |

## Learning Objectives

- Diagnosis based on individual accounts and on consolidated accounts.
- Study of profitability, solvency, financial structure and return (ROCE,
  ROE).
- Analysis of listed and unlisted companies.

## Targeted RNCP knowledge and skills

1. Carry out economic, regulatory, legal and tax monitoring (Finance Bill,
 CSRD directive, IFRS standards, US GAAP, AMF, etc.) in order to build a
 financial strategy that will support the organisation's activity and
 development in compliance with the national and international standards
 in force in its sector and on its market.
2. Analyse the organisation's business model, its CSR strategy and its
 market in order to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and
 risks, and to co-build its strategy and business plan with management.
3. Lead the production of financial statements (balance sheet, income
 statement and cash-flow statement) while ensuring data quality and
 compliance with standards (IFRS, GAAP, etc.) in order to produce reliable
 documents that can be shared with internal and external stakeholders and
 used as a basis for decision-making.
4. Lead the production of non-financial performance statements while
 ensuring the quality of the data included in the ESG criteria in order to
 produce reports that present the CSR strategy to internal and external
 stakeholders.
5. Analyse the organisation's financial data from the statements produced
 previously using relevant ratios (liquidity, solvency and profitability
 ratios, BFR (working-capital requirement), etc.) and synthesise the data
 in order to assess its financial soundness, solvency and performance.
6. Design the company's financial strategy (medium- and long-term financial
 planning, budgets, cash plan) according to the company's strategic
 choices and CSR policy, in order to agree common objectives with senior
 management, identify the means to achieve them and secure the company's
 activity.
7. Translate the company's CSR strategy into ESG criteria and lead the
 implementation of their measurement in order to support the company's CSR
 policy, measure it and produce the non-financial performance statements.
8. Design and run the budgeting process in coordination with the
 organisation's various functions and with management control, reflecting
 the defined strategy in order to achieve the financial objectives and
 ensure its financial performance.

# Sessions

Centred on an _active_ learning approach, the course turns students into
players^[_[The Multiplayer Classroom: Designing Coursework as a Game, Lee Sheldon](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/48805975-the-multiplayer-classroom)_],
modules into quests, assessments into experience points (XP), and skills into
levels to be reached.

## Session plan

The course runs over **3 days of 6 hours of teaching (360 minutes each,
1,080 minutes, i.e. 18 h in total)**, divided into **3 main quests**. Breaks
are not counted. The minute-by-minute detail is in the
[planning](planning.qmd).

Each quest begins with **20 to 30 minutes of live theory** (included in its
duration); the reference pages serve as **pre-reading** (at most 45 minutes
per evening).

**Exams.** The 1 h and 3 h 30 exams are **outside the 18 h**: they take place
in a separate session. During the three days, only the "boss" cases and XP
assess the students.

| Block | Duration | Session | Topics covered |
|-------|------:|--------|----------------|
| D1-B1 | 15 min | Day 1 — Kick-off | Game rules, teams, the 6 BdF steps |
| D1-B2 | 110 min | Day 1 — Q1: [The Temple of Balance Sheets](modules/01-temple-bilans.qmd) | Balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement |
| D1-B3 | 100 min | Day 1 — Q2: [The Consolidated Archives](modules/02-archives-consolidees.qmd) | Consolidation, scope, intragroup eliminations |
| D1-B4 | 135 min | Day 1 — Q3: [The Diagnostic Detective](modules/03-detective-diagnostic.qmd) | The 6 BdF steps, full diagnosis of an SME, boss |
| D2-B1 | 120 min | Day 2 — Q4: [The Profitability Arenas](modules/04-arenes-rentabilite.qmd) | ROCE, ROE, DuPont, financial leverage |
| D2-B2 | 105 min | Day 2 — Q5: [The Business-Model Cartographers](modules/05-cartographes-modele-eco.qmd) | SWOT, Business Model Canvas, CSR/ESG |
| D2-B3 | 135 min | Day 2 — Q6: [The Council of Sages](modules/06-conseil-sages.qmd) | BdF rating, listed vs unlisted companies, valuation, boss |
| D3-B1 | 100 min | Day 3 — Q7: [The Market Watchers](modules/07-veilleurs-marche.qmd) | Regulatory monitoring (CSRD, IFRS, AMF) |
| D3-B2 | 110 min | Day 3 — Q8: [The Strategy Architects](modules/08-architectes-strategie.qmd) | Financial planning, BFR, cash |
| D3-B3 | 140 min | Day 3 — Q9: [The Guardians of Non-Financial Performance](modules/09-gardiens-extra-financier.qmd) | ESG, DPEF (non-financial performance statement), CSRD, final boss |
| D3-B4 | 10 min | Day 3 — Closing | Levels, badges, debrief |

Reference pages: [Banque de France method](modules/banque-france.qmd),
[financial statements](modules/etats-financiers.qmd),
[performance](modules/performances.qmd),
[financial structure](modules/structure-fi.qmd),
[liquidity](modules/liquidite.qmd),
[rating](modules/banque-france-cotation.qmd),
[formulas](modules/formules.qmd) and [glossary](glossaire.qmd).

## Game theme: "The Finance Strategists"

Students play junior financial analysts in a fictional firm called
**"StratFin Corp"**. Their mission: climb the ranks to become **Experts in
Financial Strategy**, by completing quests, collaborating, and producing
strategic deliverables.

## Structure of the 3 days (18 h)

Each day is divided into **3 main quests**, with **team activities**,
**end-of-day bosses** (practical cases) and **XP** awarded for each activity.

### Day 1: Exploring the financial statements (360 min)

**Objective**: players discover the basics of financial diagnosis and the
foundations of the Banque de France methodology, a prerequisite for analysing
consolidated accounts.

- **Prerequisites**: notions of general accounting (balance sheet, income
  statement).
- **Pre-reading (≈ 15 min)**: [The three financial statements](modules/etats-financiers.qmd).
- **Blocks**: kick-off (15), Q1 (110), Q2 (100), Q3 + boss (135).
- **End-of-day deliverable**: oral presentation of the diagnosis of
  MEDITECH SAS and a credit recommendation (10 min per presentation).
- **XP**: Q1 +100, Q2 +150, Q3 +200.

### Day 2: Performance and strategy analysis (360 min)

**Objective**: players learn to assess a company's performance and strategy.

- **Prerequisites**: having attended Day 1 (or having read the reference
  pages [performance](modules/performances.qmd) and
  [formulas](modules/formules.qmd)).
- **Evening preparation (≈ 45 min)**:
  - read the [performance](modules/performances.qmd) page and the sheet of
    main ratios ([formulas](modules/formules.qmd));
  - collect, from the annual report chosen on Day 1, the data needed to
    compute equity, EBIT, financial debt and BFR (working-capital
    requirement);
  - compute at least 2 ratios and note their interpretation.
- **Blocks**: Q4 (120), Q5 (105), Q6 + boss (135).
- **End-of-day deliverable**: comparative study of a listed company
  (CAC 40) and an unlisted SME in the same sector, presented in 5 min per
  team.
- **XP**: Q4 +150, Q5 +150, Q6 +200.

### Day 3: Monitoring, ESG and financial strategy (360 min)

**Objective**: players become strategists able to integrate ESG and
regulatory issues.

- **Prerequisites**: having attended Day 2; the annual report chosen on Day 1
  is reused.
- **Evening preparation (≈ 45 min)**:
  - read the Déclaration de Performance Extra-Financière (DPEF,
    non-financial performance statement) or the CSR section of the annual
    report;
  - complete with a short news article (green bonds, carbon tax or
    sustainable finance);
  - identify a CSR/ESG initiative and its possible financial impact (costs,
    image, funding, profitability), in at most 5 slides or one page.
- **Blocks**: Q7 (100), Q8 (110), Q9 + final boss (140), closing (10).
- **End-of-day deliverable**: defence of a strategic report integrating ESG
  and finance; the "at home" part of Q9 (cost-of-capital adjustment,
  1.5-page report) completes the quest grade.
- **XP**: Q7 +150, Q8 +150, Q9 +250.

## Module assessment

In this course, students move through a _gamified_ learning universe. Every
activity, whether an individual mission, group work or a presentation, earns
**experience points (XP)**. These XP reflect engagement, the quality of the
work and progress in acquiring skills. The system is structured in
**levels**: _Junior Analyst_, _Confirmed Analyst_, _Financial Strategist_,
and finally _Experts in Financial Strategy_.

As they accumulate XP, students unlock **badges** recognising their technical
skills (diagnosis, ratios, ESG), their collaborative spirit and their
strategic ability. This system fosters motivation, active participation and
gradual skill development, while making learning more immersive and
stimulating.

The XP per quest, the levels, the badges and the calculation of the final
grade (40% XP, 60% exam) are detailed on the
[Assessment](evaluation.qmd) page. The 1 h and 3 h 30 exams are outside the
18 h.
